steps.name: Film Studio Boss
steps.text: Founded over a decade ago, Excelsior Studios has spent more than ten years building its business and has produced many popular late-night movies.

steps.name: Film Studio Boss
steps.text: At our peak, we were shooting day-in, day-out. Every midnight screening at every theater was one of ours.

steps.name: Film Studio Boss
steps.text: However, ticket sales have been dropping these past two years. We've had more than a few box-office busts.

steps.name: Film Studio Boss
steps.text: Even soap opera directors are refusing to work with us now. They say we're an 'unserious studio' that 'only produces boring gore.'

steps.name: Film Studio Boss
steps.text: And it's hard to deny that our management is as lacking as our funds. Truth is, there's no way we'll ever be making another movie.

steps.name: Film Studio Boss
steps.text: Even I'm forced to admit that no one wants gory, violent films these days. We've lost our audience.

steps.name: Film Studio Boss
steps.text: I've put my heart and soul into our work, and I know you all have too. However, today I regret to inform you that...

steps.name: Film Studio Boss
steps.text: Excelsior Studios will be shutting down next week.

steps.name: Cinematographer
steps.text: Ugh—all that melodrama, and in the end they aren't giving us a penny in severance! If they don't wanna pay us, then just say so!

steps.name: Script Supervisor
steps.text: How are they supposed to pay us if they're bankrupt?

steps.name: Cinematographer
steps.text: You bought that nonsense? He's shuffling money from one hand to the other as we speak, getting ready to set up another production company.

steps.name: Cinematographer
steps.text: If you don't believe me, just read last week's newspapers. This is all common knowledge!

steps.name: Script Supervisor
steps.text: If he's going to set up a new studio, why wouldn't he just rehire us to work for that one?

steps.name: Cinematographer
steps.text: He's betting on mainstream blockbusters. We make our money from slasher films. There's no room for us in his plans.

steps.name: Script Supervisor
steps.text: *sigh* Then where will we be able to find any work?

steps.name: Script Supervisor
steps.text: What are you hanging your head for, Tippi?

steps.name: Script Supervisor
steps.text: Haven't you worked for several major studio films over the past two years? You've made a name for yourself, so you at least shouldn't have any trouble finding work.

steps.name: Script Supervisor
steps.text: ...Tippi?

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: No, I have to go talk to the boss.

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: Boss, I want to talk to you about something—

steps.name: Film Studio Boss
steps.text: Tippi, I already explained this very clearly in our last meeting. I don't have a dime to my name.

steps.name: Film Studio Boss
steps.text: Obviously, I'd love to pay you if I could, but... the studio's broke. There's no money to give you.

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: That's not what I'm here about.

steps.name: Film Studio Boss
steps.text: ...Oh? Then, what, did you just want to say goodbye?

steps.name: Film Studio Boss
steps.text: I appreciate it, but you might want to hold off on that.

steps.name: Film Studio Boss
steps.text: I'm just shutting this studio down, not leaving the film business for good. I'm sure we'll meet again on another set soon enough.

spans.text: studio down, not leaving the film business for good. I'm sure we'll meet again on another set soon enough.

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: No, it's not that either.

steps.name: Film Studio Boss
steps.text: Then why do you want to speak to me?

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: I just wanted to know what plans you have for the backgrounds in storage.

steps.name: Film Studio Boss
steps.text: ...The backgrounds?

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: The ones we made for the films. They should be stored in the prop room behind the office.

steps.name: Film Studio Boss
steps.text: Oh, right, those. Finance just came to me two days ago and told me that it had cost us 1,530,000 bucks to store all that wood during the past two years.

steps.name: Film Studio Boss
steps.text: 1,530,000 gold certificates. I don't even think it's worth the 30,000 certs it would cost to ship them to the lumber yard.

steps.name: Film Studio Boss
steps.text: So I called somebody to come take care of them. No idea if they'll take them to the lumber yard or chop them up for firewood. Doesn't matter to me.

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: But we all invested so much time creating these together... And they hold so many memories for our audience, too.

steps.name: Film Studio Boss
steps.text: Who cares about backgrounds made by a feckless film studio?

steps.name: Film Studio Boss
steps.text: Tippi, you're a skilled background painter. Your work in Bloodthirsty Midnight was nothing short of astounding.

spans.text: Tippi, you're a skilled background painter. Your work in

steps.name: Film Studio Boss
steps.text: To be honest, when we looked at those, they looked so real we couldn't believe they were actually just some painted wood.

steps.name: Film Studio Boss
steps.text: That's what makes you stand out from the rest. You're the best artist in the crew. People actually like the stuff you make.

steps.name: Film Studio Boss
steps.text: But Bloodthirsty Midnight lost me 30 million bucks. It's the biggest flop I've ever had.

spans.text: lost me 30 million bucks. It's the biggest flop I've ever had.

steps.name: Film Studio Boss
steps.text: The screenwriter, the director, the cinematographer, the actors—not one of them was up to the task. What use were your beautifully painted backgrounds then?

steps.name: Film Studio Boss
steps.text: If the public doesn't like what they see, then we won't make any money, and no more movies will get made. That's just how it works.

steps.name: Film Studio Boss
steps.text: Tastes can evolve. After more than ten years making horror films, it's time for me to broaden my audience.

steps.name: Film Studio Boss
steps.text: Don't you want more people to recognize your work? If so, then you need to keep aiming higher.

steps.name: Film Studio Boss
steps.text: Other people may not know your background, Tippi, but I do. Go ask your grandfather about all this. He'd agree with me.

steps.name: Film Studio Boss
steps.text: If folks had just looked out for the studio and kept up with the times, we wouldn't end up like this.

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: Well... can I at least keep one of the backgrounds?

steps.name: Film Studio Boss
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Film Studio Boss
steps.text: The studio paid you to paint those, filmed them, and distributed tens of thousands of copies of them into the market.

steps.name: Film Studio Boss
steps.text: Everything involved in the production is the property of Excelsior Studios, including, of course, the backgrounds.

steps.name: Film Studio Boss
steps.text: You can look through the Columbian IP laws yourself. It's written in black and white.

steps.name: Cinematographer
steps.text: Everyone, a final toast before we go our separate ways. Tippi, you can have grape juice instead.

steps.name: Script Supervisor & Tippi
steps.text: Here here.

steps.name: Cinematographer
steps.text: C'mon Tippi, don't be so down in the dumps.

steps.name: Cinematographer
steps.text: You may not have realized, but plenty of people knew that the boss was actually planning on investing in those 'box office blockbusters'. It was just a matter of when.

steps.name: Cinematographer
steps.text: As for that background you wanted... trust me, the ones you're going to paint in the future will all be so much better.

steps.name: Cinematographer
steps.text: The heads of the big studios know you're skilled. And they've got plenty of resources, so you'll have plenty of chances to fulfill your dream.

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: Well, what studios are you guys going to go work for after this?

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: I know a few good producers, maybe they could—

steps.name: Cinematographer
steps.text: Me? I'll pass. Guess I'll just find some ad agency to work for. Some of them love hiring ex-cinematographers.

steps.name: Cinematographer
steps.text: Haha. That is, of course, assuming they haven't seen any of my previous works.

steps.name: Cinematographer
steps.text: And what about you, Eileen? You've been looking at job ads for six months now. Have you found a new gig yet?

steps.name: Script Supervisor
steps.text: Ugh. Was I that obvious?!

steps.name: Cinematographer
steps.text: I've used the same job website before, so the second I accidently glanced at your screen, I knew.

steps.name: Script Supervisor
steps.text: I-I see.

steps.name: Script Supervisor
steps.text: To be honest, I don't know what I'm going to do next...

steps.name: Script Supervisor
steps.text: These past four years, all I've done was operate the clapperboard and log shot numbers.

steps.name: Script Supervisor
steps.text: Now, if you tell me I have to go do some other kind of work, I can't even really picture that. Maybe I'll go back home and study a new trade. Maybe a quiet, stable life would better suit me.

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: ...So you're both leaving Wrankwood?

steps.name: Cinematographer
steps.text: Tippi, I just happened to get into this dirty business a bit sooner than you, but I'm nowhere near as talented or lucky as you.

steps.name: Cinematographer
steps.text: Being able to make a living as a professional cameraman is more than enough for me. It doesn't much matter if that happens in Wrankwood or not.

steps.name: Cinematographer
steps.text: To most of us, working at Excelsior Studios was just a job.

steps.name: Cinematographer
steps.text: Sometimes you put your all into a job, telling yourself not to quit, only to realize it just wasn't the right fit. And that's perfectly normal.

steps.name: Cinematographer
steps.text: So many people come to Wrankwood to 'make it big', but few ever do.

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: But I really treasured my time working with all of you!

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: I don't think you're any less talented than the folks who do big mainstream flicks—if anything, you've got more heart than those studio types.

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: Which is why I wanted to stay here and work with you. I really wanted us to shoot a few more films together...

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: I don't see why the boss has to get rid of you like this!

steps.name: Script Supervisor
steps.text: It's so sweet of you to say so, Tippi, and that's exactly what I'll be missing in the future, not anything else.

steps.name: Script Supervisor
steps.text: At first, I only came to Wrankwood because people loved my acting on the school play. But once I got here, I discovered I was average at best.

steps.name: Script Supervisor
steps.text: But you, Tippi, with your talent, you'll definitely write... err... paint your name in Wrankwood history.

steps.name: Script Supervisor
steps.text: You were born for this job. You need to stay here.

steps.name: Script Supervisor
steps.text: And if you ever end up on that podium to accept an award, I can already see myself bragging to the folks back home that I once worked with you!

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: But... but...

steps.name: Cinematographer
steps.text: Hey, does anyone remember we were here to have fun and cuss out the boss together?

steps.name: Cinematographer
steps.text: The bar is empty right now. Why don't we put on a movie, have a few drinks, and chat for a bit, like old times.

steps.name: Script Supervisor
steps.text: Maybe we could let Tippi pick the movie this time?

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: Let me think... How about we go with the first film we worked on together? Bad Boy?

spans.text: Let me think... How about we go with the first film we worked on together?

steps.name: Cinematographer
steps.text: No. I like to think I have some taste. Why would I want to watch my own terrible film?

spans.text: No. I like to think I have
taste. Why would I want to watch my own terrible film?

steps.name: Script Supervisor
steps.text: This is our last time together, Matthew. Let her watch what she wants.

steps.name: Cinematographer
steps.text: ....Fine. Bad Boy it is then.
The old, color-cast projector hums as its cooling fan spins. The three of them sit around a small round table, watching the end credits roll slowly.

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: ...Pfft.

steps.name: Script Supervisor
steps.text: Haha... hahahahaha!

steps.name: Cinematographer
steps.text: That was so Friedkin cringe! That guy kept on slashing people until he stood at the awards podium!

steps.name: Cinematographer
steps.text: Why didn't anyone say anything to the screenwriter during filming?! What were they thinking?

steps.name: Script Supervisor
steps.text: I... I don't know. Maybe the director just wanted another gory flick. Man. My stomach hurts from laughing so much!

steps.name: Script Supervisor
steps.text: And... what kind of camera lens were you using, dude? I could see inside that guy's nostrils and count his nose hairs!

steps.name: Cinematographer
steps.text: I... I have no idea! We did so many takes! How did that one make it out of the editing room?!

spans.text: I... I have no idea! We did so many takes! How did
one make it out of the editing room?!

steps.name: Script Supervisor
steps.text: Ugh! That was absolute trash! Hahaha!

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: Hahahaha... right! And look at that background! All smeared! I pulled three all-nighters in a row rushing to finish it.

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: Every time I watch this, I want to reach inside the screen and scrub my name from the credits.

steps.name: Cinematographer
steps.text: Wait, you've actually watched this multiple times? I don't think I've seen it even once!

steps.name: Script Supervisor
steps.text: Tippi, do you actually enjoy watching your own movies at home?

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: N-no! I just really like the last scene of this one.

steps.name: Cinematographer
steps.text: That ridiculous final scene? Hahahaa.....

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: I like the background in it. That rough-looking podium.

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: Maybe you don't remember, but that background... the entire cast and crew signed it on the back.

steps.name: Script Supervisor
steps.text: Wait... really?

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: Yeah. This was the first movie I worked on here. Back then they were already saying the studio was about to go under.

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: The original cast we had was afraid the studio wouldn't make payroll, and quit right before we started shooting. Then the investors all pulled out.

steps.name: Cinematographer
steps.text: Yeah, I remember now. We all thought that would be our last movie. It felt like just finishing it was a victory in itself.

steps.name: Script Supervisor
steps.text: If I remember correctly, I snagged the best-looking extra and turned him into our impromptu leading man.

steps.name: Cinematographer
steps.text: And when the filming was finally finished, we signed that background together.

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: We still made it, right? And the movie actually did pretty well at the box office—some theaters even put us in daytime slots for the first time!

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: We were forced to add those extra gory scenes to cater to our audience, but we never thought they'd love it so much.

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: We kept the studio running for two years before it shut down... Still, we did save it once. We're not failures!

steps.name: Cinematographer
steps.text: So... you still want us to stick around?

steps.name: Script Supervisor
steps.text: I know you're trying to cheer us up, Tippi, but there's no saving the studio this time around.

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: No, it's not that. I respect your decision.

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: It's just, I just... before we all part ways, I want to see the signatures on that background one last time.

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: ...Are you coming with me?
A weak glow reveals a huge pile of prop, covered with dust. Once filmed, they were all left here untouched.

steps.name: Cinematographer
steps.text: *cough cough cough cough* It's so dusty in here! I can barely breathe!

steps.name: Script Supervisor
steps.text: (whispers) Keep it down, Matthew! There are guards at the gate. We can't let them know we're here!

steps.name: Cinematographer
steps.text: (covers mouth) Hrrgh....ugh.

steps.name: Script Supervisor
steps.text: (whispers) All of these backgrounds piled up are taller than me several times over... I never realized we'd made so many films!

steps.name: Cinematographer
steps.text: (whispers) Hah! You know what's more unbelievable? If you just stacked your shot logs and my reels together they'd be taller than either of us.

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: (whispers) Hey! I found it!
The three of them walk up to a background. It's been two years, but its paint still looks fresh.

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: Let's flip it over.

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: Wow. Our glorious achievement.

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: This 'Final Movie' wasn't our final one. We saved this place.

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: These mountains of backgrounds are proof of all the work we did together. They could easily pave the entire Walk of Fame.

steps.name: Matthew
steps.text: (sobs)

steps.name: Eileen
steps.text: Matthew... are you alright?

steps.name: Matthew
steps.text: I'm... I'm fine. I'm just... a little drunk.
The big man forces his sobs down as Eileen's eyes swell up with tears.
Tippi takes her friends' hands and slowly walks toward the background.

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: Just like the story of Bad Boy, we've now busted out of prison, wiped out all the villains in the hall, and stepped onto the podium—

spans.text: , we've now busted out of prison, wiped out all the villains in the hall, and stepped onto the podium—

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: And now we have Wrankwood's Best Cinematographer, Mr. Matthew Thomas! And Wrankwood's Best Script Supervisor, Miss Eileen Hunter! Would you two like to say a few words?

steps.name: Matthew
steps.text: Err...

steps.name: Eileen
steps.text: (shouting) Screw you, Excelsior Studios!

steps.name: Eileen
steps.text: (shouting even louder) Eat shit, Wrankwood!

steps.name: Matthew
steps.text: Uh... Screw you, Excelsior Studios!

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: Eat shit, Wrankwood!
Their voices linger in the warehouse for a long time. Only after the echoes completely fade do the three of them burst into uncontrollable laughter.

steps.name: Matthew
steps.text: Hahaha. I'm drunk. We're all drunk!

steps.name: Eileen
steps.text: Just now, all our years of filming movies together flashed through my mind. Time really flies!

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: Yeah. It's like a dream.
Tippi grabs tightly to Matthew and Eileen's hands and slowly raises their arms.

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: My friends, now it is time for us to close the final curtain.

steps.name: Matthew
steps.text: (Raises arm)

steps.name: Eileen
steps.text: (Raises arm)

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: If only we had a spotlight...
Before Tippi can finish speaking, a sharp beam of light hits the three of them, so bright they cannot even keep their eyes open.

steps.name: Security Guard
steps.text: Who's there? Don't move!

steps.name: Security Guard
steps.text: Hands up!

steps.name: Eileen
steps.text: Damn. We were a bit too loud. Should we run?

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: ...We have to!

steps.name: Matthew
steps.text: Wait!

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: Wh-What's wrong?

steps.name: Eileen
steps.text: They're coming!

steps.name: Matthew
steps.text: Well, now that we've been spotted, might as well take this podium with us, right?
Tippi takes a deep breath. She can sense the beam of light growing in intensity as it nears them.

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: I like the way you think.
That night, a giant background, with a huge podium painted on it, rolled through the streets of Wrankwood.
Even in Wrankwood, where strange happenings are aplenty, a scene like this was surreal. People gathered around, taking photos of it.
People took shot of the podium passing Wrankwood's Walk of Fame, the Hall of Fame, and the Film Plaza...
But, for some unknown reason, no one got a clear shot of the people carrying it. There were just three vague, shadowy outlines in those photos.
Fortunately, the public didn't look too closely into the identities of these three, and the entire matter became fodder for dinner table conversations.
After all, so many people come to Wrankwood to 'make it big', but few ever do.
